profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC15 data center at 44780 Performance Circle, Ashburn, Virginia, immediately adjacent to Equinix's DC12 building on Performance Circle inside Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC15 facility page lists this as a two story building with a precast concrete exterior totaling 115,604 square feet (10,740 square meters), slightly larger than DC12 next door. The page publishes N+1 UPS redundancy and N+1 generator redundancy, with generators rated for 30 hours or more of runtime at full load, 240v/415v power distribution, and a minimum cabinet density of 5kVA. Cooling redundancy is listed as N+20% rather than the flat N+1 figure Equinix publishes for DC12, and floor load capacity is listed at 250 pounds per square foot. Fire protection combines double interlock pre-action suppression with both aspirated, HSSD or VESDA style, and non-aspirated detection. Security is listed as 24/7 with biometric entrance mantraps and video recording surveillance, and Equinix's DC15 page does not list HECVAT among its certifications, unlike the DC12, DC13, and DC21 pages nearby on the same campus. The eight certifications Equinix does list for DC15 are HIPAA, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, ISO 9001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II, alongside a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment. Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC15 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project attracted into Loudoun County helped seed the interconnected cluster that followed, including Virginia's early MAE East internet exchange. Equinix opened its first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Data Center Dynamics describes the resulting corridor as roughly 10 million square feet of built data center space region wide, consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power across all operators combined, not Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group, and at least one building number appearing in public address records for the area, DC17, has no active linked page on Equinix's own site at present. Equinix markets its Ashburn buildings collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, along with Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products, without singling out DC15's own peering density or customer roster.

reading.body:
DC15 is a 115,604-square-foot facility in Ashburn's Data Center Alley, part of Equinix's multi-building campus in Loudoun County. Equinix does not publish DC15's power capacity or specific certifications, though the broader Ashburn campus is positioned to serve one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast and historically anchors the region's roughly 10 million square feet of total data center space. Without disclosed megawatts, no estimate of AI training rack density can be made for this building.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power capacity; those 23 total 1,375 MW. Equinix Ashburn DC15 is not among the published figures. The operator's own Ashburn DC2, described as representative of the campus's general specifications, declares a minimum cabinet density of 4 kVA and N+1 power redundancy, but these specifications are not confirmed for DC15 itself.

The absence of published capacity makes this building's significance to AI scaling opaque from available data. Data Center Alley's historical role in internet infrastructure and Equinix's dense interconnection footprint matter only if DC15's power allocation to compute-intensive workloads becomes visible; the current specifications disclose no basis to assess that.
